easy.def: A rough, twisted bump on a tree.
examples: The tree has a gnarl.
A gnarl is a lump.
The gnarl was rough.

more.def: A rough, twisted lump or knot on a tree trunk or branch.
examples: The old oak tree had a huge gnarl on its trunk.
A gnarl twisted the branch.
The gnarl looked like a face.

easy.def: Twisted and rough, like an old tree.
examples: The gnarled tree was old.
He had gnarled hands.
A gnarled branch hung low.

more.def: Rough, twisted and bumpy, usually from being very old, like the branches of an ancient tree.
examples: Birds nested in the gnarled branches of the ancient oak.
The old fisherman had gnarled hands from years of pulling in heavy nets.
A gnarled root pushed up through the path and tripped me.
The wolf gnashed its teeth.
He gnashed his teeth.
The dragon gnashed.

more.def: To grind or bite your teeth together, as a sign of anger or pain.
examples: The wolf in the story gnashed its teeth.
He gnashed his teeth in frustration at the broken toy.
The monster gnashed its teeth and growled.
A gnat flew by.
Gnats are tiny.
A gnat bit me.

more.def: A tiny flying insect that often flies in swarms.
examples: A gnat buzzed around my ear.
Swarms of gnats flew over the pond.
The gnat is too small to see well.

easy.def: To chew on something hard again and again.
examples: The dog will gnaw a bone.
Mice gnawed the box.
Beavers gnaw wood.

more.def: To keep biting or chewing on something hard.
examples: The puppy gnawed a bone all afternoon.
Beavers gnaw trees to build dams.
A mouse gnawed a hole in the box.

easy.def: A tiny old man with a pointy hat in stories.
examples: The gnome lives in the garden.
A gnome had a red hat.
We have a gnome.

more.def: A small, make-believe man with a pointed hat who is said to live underground or in gardens.
examples: A gnome statue stood in the garden.
In the story, a gnome guarded the gold.
The gnome wore a bright red hat and a long beard.

easy.def: A big animal with horns and a beard.
examples: A gnu ate grass.
The gnu has horns.
We saw a gnu.

more.def: A large African antelope with a shaggy beard and curved horns, also called a wildebeest.
examples: A herd of gnus crossed the plain.
The gnu has a long face and a shaggy mane.
Thousands of gnus travel together each year.
